intro.title: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with two input fields to explore the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components in React. You will learn how React manages form data by comparing state-driven controlled inputs with directly accessed uncontrolled ones. The core concepts involve using React's useState hook for controlled components and the useRef hook to access DOM elements for uncontrolled components. You will implement both patterns in TypeScript, ensuring type safety for your input values and references. By the end, you'll understand when to use each approach for handling form data in your applications.
intro.usecase: Understanding controlled vs uncontrolled components is essential when building interactive forms in applications like user registration, checkout flows, or settings panels. In a controlled approach, React manages form state—ideal for real-time validation in sign-up forms where each keystroke must be validated. Uncontrolled components are useful for file upload inputs or search filters where you only need the final value on submission. This distinction helps developers choose the right pattern for scenarios like dashboard filters (controlled for immediate UI updates) versus simple contact forms (uncontrolled for less overhead).
